evidence:
MECHANICAL HALF. instruction.md:11,13,15 names exactly three shipped paths: /instructions/hireops_rules.md, /instructions/integration.md, /assets/seed_data.json. All exist under environment/ and environment/Dockerfile:14-16 does 'COPY instructions/ /instructions/', 'COPY assets/ /assets/' and chmod -R a+rX on both. The task Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template Dockerfile (sha256 0a75419e...67d1 both). seed_data.json parses (28549 bytes, sha256 a1c65c80...3740). No other asset path is named in the brief, notes, app_context or judge prompts. task.toml artifacts=["/app","/assets"] matches the staged contract; test.sh is template-identical (bd682592...aa5be). instruction.md:15 says /assets and /instructions are unavailable at runtime and to copy what is needed into /app; the golden does exactly that (solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json; db.js:10 reads it relative to __dirname; solve.sh:35 copies app/ into /app; no app.db shipped).

CONTENT VS BRIEF AND NOTES. instruction.md:15 lists 'people, jobs, applications, messages, notes and read markers'; seed keys are users(10), jobs(3), applications(16), messages(127), notes(3), reads(6), plus stages, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size. hireops_rules.md section 9 claims three jobs with ordered cards, one long conversation, a few notes, read markers counted from the first message, candidate wording and page size 30 in the same file: all true (thread_page_size=30; candidate_status_labels exactly equal the section 7 table; stages APPLIED..REJECTED in the section 3 order). The 10 user emails/roles match instruction.md:17 and app_context.md:10-19 one-for-one; no password in seed, password given publicly. Job manager_id/recruiter_id reference users of the right role; interview_limit 3/2/3 within 1-50 and seeded Interview counts 2/3, 1/2, 1/3 do not exceed them; positions are contiguous 1..n per job+stage; the one rejected card (APP-301) has rejected_from SCREEN and a non-blank reason; no orphan ids; message timestamps strictly ascending per conversation; read_count values never exceed the conversation length. The seed's generated_note points to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, which exists.

CONTENT VS JUDGES. functional/prompt.md:25 (Z) and judge.toml:335,407: Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread on her Product Designer conversation -> APP-301 has 3 messages (REC3, CAN3, REC3) and reads gives USR-CAN3 read_count 2, so exactly one message by others is unread: correct. Seeded Platform Engineer order Applied: Greta Lindqvist(1), Ade Bello(2), Marco Rossi(3); Screen: Priya Nair(1), Samuel Ortiz(2): matches seed positions. Noor's card note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' is APP-101's note verbatim. app_context.md:29-30 and functional judge.toml:317, polish judge.toml:32,41: Noor Haddad's Platform Engineer conversation is long with 120 messages -> APP-101 has exactly 120 messages, numbered (#001)..(#120) in order, so latest-30 and repeated earlier loads (30/60/90/120) are testable; 'Platform Engineer' disambiguates Noor's second application APP-302 (Product Designer). Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation (functional prompt.md:39 fallback) is APP-201 on JOB-DATA, whose manager is USR-MGR2 Bill Okafor, consistent with the U/T rows naming Bill as that job's manager. Visual prompt.md:14 needs a seeded job with cards in several stages: JOB-PLAT has Applied/Screen/Interview/Offer cards. Polish prompt.md:16 forbids touching Lena's conversation, protecting the Z baseline. Rafael read_count 120 on APP-101 means he starts with 0 unread there, so the scrolled-up 'one new message' row is well defined.

GOLDEN USES THE SAME SEMANTICS. db.js:82-83 maps read_count to the id of the read_count-th message; index.js:133 counts messages with id > last_read and sender != user, yielding Lena=1 from the seed. Raw evidence: raw-evidence-index.json lists six artifacts, all present with matching sha256, and every matching_source_files hash (including solution/app/src/seed_data.json a1c65c80...) equals the frozen bytes; results/workspace.json records passed groups including 'conversation: latest 30 shown, earlier messages load in order and keep place' and 'candidate read model is private; thread access by role; thread paging 30 at a time'. This is scripted golden evidence, not a configured judge run.

ADVERSARIAL PROBES. Broken app that could pass: one that ignores the seed or hard-codes a demo would fail Z/D (seeded order, Noor's note, Lena=1), the 120-message paging rows and the seeded-account sign-ins, because every graded seeded fact is present and checkable in the asset. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app that stores positions 0-based, uses its own ids, title-case stage names or a different read-marker representation still produces the same visible order/counts; only a misreading of read_count (which hireops_rules.md section 9 defines explicitly) would change Lena's count, which is a legitimate model error. No seeded fact the judges assert is absent from or contradicted by the asset. Not exercised: no full configured judge run was observed reading these seeded facts; that is a separate runtime-evidence gap owned by workload/grading rows and does not affect whether the assets match.
